Title: The !Ventrue need a few good vampires...

Messages.Author: Alex Broadhead
Messages.Body:
Howdy,

Continuing along with my unprovoked, unsolicited, and very probably
unappetizing run of card suggestions for my ex-favorite clan, here's
some stats, some gaps, and some more filler. (Yes, Mike, we know -
all holes must be filled!)

!Ventrue Crypt + Suggestions

Samson dom 2

Juan Cali aus for 3
>Prince Michael FOR 3 vic, -

Ingrid Russo DOM for 4
Peter Blaine aus dom for 4 *
>Vivian Wang, Apostate aus for 4 val

>Alexander, Toady to the Umbradomo AUS FOR 5 Bishop, *
Billy AUS dom for 5
Gerard aus dom for 5 obt
Vincent Day, Paladin and Paragon aus dom for 5 pot, tha *

Dylan aus dom for 6 cel, pro *
>Evelyn Milk AUS DOM FOR 6 nec
Marlene, The Infernalist AUS DOM for 6 dem, tha
Vanessa aus DOM FOR 6 pre

Edward Neally aus DOM FOR 7 pre **
Dominique AUS dom FOR 7 ani, vic *

Gustav Mallenhous AUS DOM for 8 obt, Priscus **

Kyle Strathcona, Cardinal of Canada AUS DOM for 9 POT, PRE, Cardinal
*
Quentin AUS DOM FOR 9 cel, obt, Bishop *

Lazverinus, Thrall of Lambach AUS DOM FOR 10 POT, pro, Archbishop
*

7/7 7/8 10/5 16
8/9 7/9 11/8 20

Prince Michael
Clan: Ventrue Antitribu
Capacity: 3
Disciplines: FOR vic
Text: Sabbat: Prince Michael does not get the usual +1 stealth when
hunting.
Art: Cross of a disturbing looking gangsta rapper-ish figure and a
soccer mom. Is Drew still available?

Vivian Wang, Apostate
Clan: Ventrue Antitribu
Disciplines: aus for val
Text: Sabbat
Art: Intense Asian woman with third eye in stern pose resting hands
on the pommel of a flaming sword with point against ground. John
Bolton (Juan Cali) maybe?

Alexander, Toady to the Umbradomo
Clan: Ventrue Antitribu
Capacity: 5
Disciplines: AUS FOR
Text: Sabbat Bishop: Alexander gets an additional +1 stealth when
taking a rescue torpor action.
Art: Founding Fathers/Musketeer-ish guy with long hair, round specs,
mustache/goatee. Yet another Christopher Shy portrait.

Evelyn Milk
Clan: Ventrue Antitribu
Capacity: 6
Disciplines: AUS DOM FOR nec
Text: Sabbat
Art: Black man in expensive suit, smiling, holding a sawed-off
shotgun loosely at his side. Tim Bradstreet & Grant Goleash,
definitely.

Basically, given that the auspex/fortitude combo is what distinguishes
the clan, it seems like a good idea to me to reinforce it to the point
that it's actually usable. Dominate is so abusable that everyone
already has - so why not give the oddballs something to play with?
Thus three of the four have aus/for, with Alexander being the
centerpiece, and a good addition not only to !Ventrue, but Salubri and
HoS decks as well. Vivian is a gift to the !Salubri, but also brings
the very useful valeren discipline in clan; Sense Vitality is quite
handy, and bruise disciplines can't hurt.

Superior fortitude, so badly missed in clan, is heavily supplemented,
with three of the four (all 6-cap or below) possessing it. Evelyn is
the greatly needed 6-cap with all in-clan; his necromancy again has
synergies with the HoS, and a stealth producing discipline can't hurt
either. (I thought about giving him inferior serpentis instead of
nec...) Prince Michael may be pushing the envelope; he'd be the
smallest cap with FOR by far. I don't see his vicissitude as being
greatly useful, though the discipline can produce bruise or stealth,
and you do start to have some interesting possibilities revolving
around him and Christine Boscacci. His disadvantage should make
Hungry Coyote abuse rather more difficult, though I suppose he could
spend a lot of time Restoring himself.

So, what do you think? Balanced? Broken? Wallpaper? All of the
above? I realize the chances of even getting this many new !Ventrue
anytime soon are just about nil, but just in case, here's the official
disclaimer: White Wolf, please, steal my ideas, they're yours for the
filching!

Thanks,
Alex

Seems like if they were that good, their names would be a little more
memorable. <insert smiley thing here>

I'd be one of the first to argue that Edward, Quentin, and Lazverinus
are exceptionally good (with emphasis on the 'exception'; those three,
plus Vanessa and the rarely used Dominique constitute _all_ of the
!Ventrue with FOR), and Billy and Vanessa are certainly mainstays.
And I'd also point out that you forgot Samson and Ingrid Russo, who
are not to be left out of dominate sleaze decks. (And Gustav is quite
good too, although he falls into an awkward hole as an 8-cap without
superior fortitude.)

But what we've arrived at in saying that is this: the !Ventrue with
FOR or dom/DOM at low cap are usable, and Billy is pretty good too.
That just doesn't strike me as a ringing endorsement, much less lead
to much deck variety. I've been trying for quite some time to put
together something workable with aus/for, but the vampires just aren't
there, even with the HoS, Salubri, and !Salubri. And, in general,
there's just so much more the !Ventrue could do if they could reliably
access superior fortitude.

Anyway, I don't want this to degenerate into another, "X
clan/discipline doesn't need anymore cards, cause if they're better
they'll break it, and if they're worse they'll be wallpaper" threads.
I recently saw the !Ventrue compared to the !Salubri in terms of
suckiness (I thought it was unjustified, but they certainly ain't
powerhouses), and so I thought I'd make some suggestions towards
fixing that. Kind of like the maps some people made for the
Independent clans during the long, dark night between AH and FN...

> They have a FEW good vampires, and that's all a clan really needs. A
> few that work better together, I'd like, but as is, you can make a
> solid deck, with a few vampire dupilcates.

Howdy,

Be careful what you ask for...

So I've been saving up a bunch o' deck idea on this very discipline
combo for use in future editions of the !Ventrue Newsletter, but since
some other sucker - I mean dedicated and selfless individual - has
hijacked - I mean assumed the editorship of that august journal, I
guess there's no reason to keep 'em to myself anymore.

The first concept I actually already detailed in one of the issues,
albeit in a pretty early and basic form; it's also the one that is
most likely to benefit from dominate as well, and so the best match to
the standard !Ventrue disciplines. That was the unblockable bleeder.
You can do unblockable bleed without auspex, of course, using Cull the
Herd or Contingency Planning or some such to keep your bleeds on
target, but Revelations (and/or Ed and/or Le) is probably the best way
to go. (And you can do the unblockable part without fortitude too,
though that's even more of a stretch.) Auspex will give you Pulses
too, but there's certainly no reason not to use the dominate on your
vampires as well.

Next up: !Ventrue bruise bleed via Dawn Op. I can hear you now - why
would I need auspex for that? Well, 'cause practically _any_ combat
defense will get around Dawn Ops. Maneuver (since !Ventrue don't have
the superior fortitude for Unflinching to work), prevent, S:CE, dodge,
they'll all allow you to accept a Dawn Op without any real fear of
damage, nullifying its already pretty minor threat, in that your prey
is already getting to pick which minion blocks. If you throw AUS into
the mix, though, you can now at least Telepathic Track, making your
prey have to do whatever trick twice in a row or eat damage, while you
hopefully have prevent coming out your ears. (Thoughts at superior
wouldn't hurt either, but it's pretty expensive...) Again, no reason
not to use the dominate on your vampires either.

Another: !Ventrue rush(/intercept). Am I mad? (Yes, probably.) The
concept: Nose of the Hound plus plenty of wake and intercept. Lots
o' Restoration and blood generation (not via hunting, though), a
goodly dose of prevent, and... a shedload of Vampiric Disease and
Pulled Fangs. Rush and block with abandon - it doesn't really matter
if you do _any damage at all_ - as long as you can get to close range.
And sooner or later you will manage to hit for 1 while preventing.

Finally, the one I've done the most work on: !Ventrue 'aggressive
intercept'. The key here is Concealed Weapon. Conceal out a
Sawed-Off. Now maneuvers don't matter. Block with Melange, Eagle's
Sight, Precognition - your predator's critical offensive actions, and
pretty much anything your prey does that you can mess with that isn't
bleeding forward. (And bleeding forward if it'll hurt your grand-prey
too much, and you happen to have the Sight for it.) Use your actions
to bruise bleed forward as well (or Restore). A Sawed-Off is a great
equalizer - suddenly any minion looks a lot like Lazverinus... As
usual, dominate doesn't hurt, but it's the least critical of the
disciplines.

Anyway, I can't say that any of these concepts is a world-killer. But
they would all be a lot easier to work on if there were a few more
low-cap aus/AUS + for/FOR vampires. As it is, it's pretty much just
Juan, Peter, Billy, and a bunch of more expensive equivalents until
you hit, like, Omaya and Matthias.

And, of course, pretty much any !Ventrue deck concept would work
better if only they had access to more FOR.

Hope that helps,
Alex

Well, I suppose it's about time that I chimed in here...

The more I postulate about the relationship of the !Ventrue in this game,
the more I find the necessity of them upon other clans/bloodlines. In and
of themselves the !Ventrue are not particularly potent, at least when we
look at them in relation to a lot of other clans. Where their strength
comes from is in the ever widening addition of vampires that interact with
them.

Though the !Ventrue don't have many big FOR vampires, their are ten Ventrue
that have have auspex as well. Two of those have AUS, and all but one fit
into a 2/3 crypt (sorry, Democritus).

The !Ventrue are also good friends of the Salubri, who have excellent
vampires, and their Obeah is a wonderful addition to the arsenal.
Likewise, the !Salubri, who have struggled, and are IMO the bottomfeeders
of the Bloodlines set share similar disciplines.

Marlene works masterfully in Tremere with for decks, while Ingred is the
lynch pin of weenie dom. Lazveranus is one bad mofo, no matter what deck
he's in.

So what then are the !Ventrue missing?

Worthwhile Clan Specific cards. The !Gangrel get City Gangrel Connections,
the !Toreador get Art Scam, heck, even the !Brujah get Gang Territory.
What do the !Ventrue get? A couple of cards that change votes. That would
be nice, except that they don't have pre, which is the kingpin voting
discipline. They're really not capable of much in this department. That's
why I'd suggest:

The Right to Rule
- Unique Master, 1 pool
- !Ventrue required
- All !Ventrue gain +2 strength when in combat with a titled vampire, this
card may be burned as a D action taken by any non-titled vampire.

Inheritence
- Master, 1 pool
- !Ventrue required
- Put 3 counters on this card when it is put into play on a ready
!Ventrue. The cost for equipment may be paid with these counters.

Of Noble Birth
- Reaction/Action Modifier, 1 blood
- !Ventrue required
- Play whenever a younger titled vampire goes to torpor. That vampire
loses his or her title.

Squire
- Retainer with 4 life, 1 blood
- !Ventrue required
- A minion equipped with this retainer may opt not to strike, if he or she
does so any damage inflicted may be redirected to this retainer

As for vampires, the !Ventrue lack sufficient quantity to make a diverse
deck. Sure a deck with 5 Lazveranus and a smattering of smaller !Ventrue
is possible, but unlike the Camarilla clans, there is a far smaller pool of
vampires to pull from. Some, like the !Brujah, Lasombra and Tzimisce are

Actually, I would have said Peter was being much, much more objective
than I would have expected - in the sense of needlessly sticking to
the 'objective' measure of goodness that the formula provides, when it
seems clear to me that more subjective measures of goodness (like play
experience) are more relevant.

That he is also misusing the formula somewhat (as Norm has pointed
out, Ian's extra disciplines should be counted as a 3-pt. special, not
as N points worth of inferiors, where N is increasing with
expansions), makes this objectivity even more strange.

Anyway, however you want to term it (objective, subjective,
subjunctive, pluscuamperfecto, whatever), I just don't see a need to
reify the formula, especially given the fact that it has evolved
several times now. It seems clear that not all disciplines or
discipline combos are equal. The formula gives a decent benchmark for
approximate power (though it sounds to me like Curevei may have a
better one, so perhaps more evolution is ahead), but it's not a
substitute for designer judgement. Put another way: since when does
'correctness' matter, unless you don't trust the designers, in which
case, I'd argue, no amount of correctness will help.

Re: Prince Michael

> > I'd be perfectly happy with a 3 point FOR vamp, m'self.

As I pointed out in the initial post, I figured Prince Mike might be
controversial. But despite all the back-and-forth, I still don't
really have a hard-and-fast reason why. All the usual suspects have
been mentioned (Force of Will, Daring, Kiss of Ra), and the usual
counter (there's just not much you can do with fortitude only) has
also been deployed; I guess I was hoping there might be some sharper
rationale against it. I'm still in favor of running it into
playtesting and seeing who salutes.

> I would not. Nor would I be happy with a 3 point ANI, 3 point DOM, 3 point
> OBF, 3 point OBT, 3 point DEM, 3 point CHI or the existing 3 point PRE.
>
> A 3 point POT doesn't bother me nor would a 3 point VIC.

As to the other 3-caps, here's my subjectivity:

ANI would be very, very scary - a 4-cap would be powerful enough;
AUS is quite balanced in Isabel, Zoe is a tad overpowered (but then
she isn't just AUS, is she);
CEL was probably a bad idea - Sarah is very strong - disposable rush
in general is pretty nasty (see ANI, POT, VIC);
CHI would be pretty much more of the same - low cap chimerstry is
where the Ravnos are at (I concur with David on cost being the
limiting factor here);
DEM would probably be a bad thing, what with superior Cloak being
in-clan;
DOM is ugly, but there's 3 4-caps already, and myriad low-cap dom, so
it might not make that much difference;
NEC gets an awful lot of play out of Rudolpho - kinda like PRO;
OBF again has 2 4-caps already, and so might not be too bad;
OBT is awfully flexible to be putting on a 3-cap, comparable to PRO;
POT already has _5_ 4-caps - it's not that a 3-cap would be any
worse, it's just that there don't need to be any more sub 5-caps.
PRE is ugly, but there are 2 4-caps who are almost as bad;
PRO is maybe a little strong in Chandler;
QUI doesn't stand on it's own real well in Harika;
SER would probably be a bad idea, comparable to DEM;
THA is pretty strong in it's _3_ sub 4-caps - I think CHI could be
comparable;
VIC I'd be a little afraid of - it's awfully easy to slap a pot or
aus master on that and make a monster;

Oh, and there should definitely be a VAL 3-cap sometime, if the
!Salubri are ever to stop sucking.

Looking it over, I guess Norm and I just tend to disagree on the value
of various disciplines, so disagreeing over FOR is par for the course;
I'm much more perplexed by my disagreement with Peter over crypt
design theory.

Hope that helps,
Alex

Hamstrung? Vampires should pay for the abilities they have, as that is how

disciplines and 20 inferior disciplines?

> Ian pays for his 6 points in disciplines he also pays 3 points for his
> special. 3 points for a special is alot. It better be damn special. Ian's
> is.

But Ian's special is "Ian has 20+ inferior disciplines". If any other
vampire has extra disciplines, they pay for them with capacity. For those
three points, Ian should have gotten 3 extra disciplines at inferior. Not
20. If his special ability was somehow actually different than simply having
20+ inferior disciplines, then he'd probably be fine. If his special was
something along the lines of:

"When Ian enters play, choose a discipline Ian doesn't have. Ian may play
cards that require the chosen discipline at the inferior level."

or

"Ian may burn 1 blood to play a card requiring a discipline he doesn't
possess at the inferior level."

Then he'd be fine. Those special abilties are functionally different than
simply having 20+ extra disciplines, which is what Ian currently has (for
all purposes, except how he interacts with 3 cards--Kiss of Ra, Speed of
Thought, Meat Hook). For all other intents and purposes, Ian simply has 20+
inferior disciplines printed on his card. Every other vampire in the game
pays (in terms of capacity) for all of their disciplines, whether they
actually use them or not. Ian does not. He simply gets 20+ inferior
disciplines, for 3 points of capacity. This is a flagrant abuse of the
standard design template.

> in disciplines. The list of vampires is not long

simply having 20+ extra inferior disciplines (excepting 3 cards out of a
thousand).

Well, no, 'cause Ian doesn't have 6 points in disciplines. He has 26+. If
his special ability was functionally different from simply having 20+
inferior disciplines printed on him, then your argument would be solid. But
as it stands, it isn't. If there was a considerably larger number of cards
like Kiss of Ra, then you'd have a strong argument. If putting a skill card
on Ian didn't grant him the superior level of that discipline, you might
have a reasonable argument. As neither of these is the case, Ian's special
ability is simply "Ian has 20+ inferior disciplines", and as such, Ian's
special ability isn't a special ability so much as simply a way to avoid
printing 20+ extra inferior disciplines on his card (in place of, say, his
portrait).

The greateness (or lack therof) is irrelevant. He is an 8 point vampire with

But for all practical purposes, he does. Again, if there were a functional
difference between his special ability and simply having 20 extra inferior

But there are multiple 4 point vamps with OBF and 4 point vamps with DOM

> A 3 point POT doesn't bother me nor would a 3 point VIC.

Messages.Author: Joshua Duffin
Messages.Body:
"XZealot" <x_ze...@cox-internet.com> wrote in message
news:v7d4e06...@corp.supernews.com...

[re Moncada versus Alexandra]

> It costs Alexandra 2 points for her untap special. It should cost Moncada
> the same.

It's probably kind of nitpicky to get this in-depth about the
point formulas for specific vampires, but anyway... Moncada's
untap special is *vastly* inferior to Alexandra's. You can use
Alexandra's *any time* during your turn. That means you can
take an additional action with it. Moncada's is only during
discard, which means you can only block with it. As defensive
play is inherently less strong than offensive, I really think
Moncada should only pay 1 point for his untap-other special.

> You are mistaken about the blood cost. It is 1 pool not 1 blood. That is
> easily worth 1 point. Especially when a potence fanatic like yourself is
> lurking around. :)

I'll grant a point for the "pool to (D) action against" ability.

That still makes him 10 in disciplines, 2 for specials, 1.5
for title, -1.5 for can't block (IMO). 12 net points for a 10
cap is standard formula these days. (Can't block is a pretty
major disadvantage on a vampire, hence my costing it at a 1.5
point disad. Even if it were only 1 point, it'd still make
him "close enough" to the formula values.)

> Here again, you are mistaken. He does not have an extra 20 points worth of
> stuff. There are many cards that Ian is useless for (i.e. Sanguine
> Instruction).

Look, fine, Ian "doesn't have" the disciplines he can play
cards for, and there are a (relatively) few cards that that
matters for. But *all other vampires* in the game do have
to "spend" their formula points on being able to play cards
for various disciplines, even if they will realistically
never actually play a single card in particular disciplines.
To claim that on Ian it should only be worth 3 points to
be able to play cards for 20 different disciplines, while
on Vincent Day it's worth 5 points to be able to play cards
for 5 different disciplines... well, it's just not sensible.
Yes, Ian Forrestal's ability is written as a special ability
instead of as discipline symbols. But that doesn't mean
it's not comparable to other vampires' inferior disciplines.

Josh

> I think you are correct. The current template doesn't take into account the
> diminishing returns of disciplines into account, but then I don't know that

It does, after a fashion, if you consider a different expression for the
current formula:

A vampire gets X-1 disciplines, where X is his capacity.
If his capacity is 5+, he gets a freebie discipline.
If his capacity is 7+, he gets another freebie.
9+ gets another freebie.

Or in other words, for vampires with no other special/title:

A vampire's capacity is set based on the number of disciplines:

1 Discipline = 2 capacity
2 D = 3 C
3 D = 4 C
4,5 D = 5 C
6 D = 6 C
7,8 D = 7 C
9 D = 8 C
10,11 D = 9 C
12 D = 10 C

Seems to follow a sort of diminishing returns pattern.

He 'gets too much stuff' according to the template. The template exists to
maintain play balance, so if play balance can be maintained outside the
template there's no reason not to break it. This seems to be the case with
Ian (and many other vampires).

(I think) I understand you position, but I don't see it as a problem: plenty
of other vampires are balanced _because_ they break the template.

> In a perfect world, all of these vampires would have been fixed. But the
> world isn't perfect, and as it is more trouble than it is worth, they don't
> get fixed. Which I accept.

Not all of these vampires are in the same situation.
Some should be fixed to keep play balance (Judah), others don't need fixing
for balance reasons, but they still break the template (Ian). Since the
template is simply a construction to help maintain play balance, there's no
point in 'fixing' those vampires that break the template and remain balanced.
It would make more sense to find a new template that better mirrors the
needs for play balance. I don't think that search is pointless, because it
would certainly prove helpfull when designing future cards.

The point was about how much the special costs, in and of itself - not
about whether it's broken or not. Specials which work together in
concert usually cost a little more than they would alone.

That's not about broken-ness; that's about how you cost a special, in
the abstract, and how specials which work together tend to cost more.

That a vampire has specials which work together well is neither here nor
there, so long as they pay appropriate costs for them. So any attempts
to compare such to other vampires are *entirely* missing the point.

Another vampire's abilities - even if they stack - may well be
appropriately costed.

>> Ian has two "abilities" that stack, in a not entirely dis-similar
>> fashion - the special, and then having a few discipline cards stacked on
>> top of him. It's not quite the same, no.
>
>If a vampires specials don't synergize then it is just a poor design,

Actually, it can be very *good* design, but it needs some careful work.
So it can end up going arse over tit, too.

Giving a vampire a random special can provide innate flexibility. For
instance, a vampire like, say:

Random Vampire
6 cap
ani chi for ser vic
+1 bleed

You're not necessarily doing too badly. (Compare Dylan.) You get an
set of inferior disciplines, and you're not particularly a bleed vampire
(you might want to fiddle with the disciplines, to taste) but at the
same time you get the flexibility and extra oomph. It adds a certain
something, so that if your Ravnos chicanery falls over, you get
something else to fall back on.

It can also let you generally introduce something to a clan without
giving them *huge* amounts of something. The Gangrel with a little
voting prowess, for instance. They provide some interesting niches to
work around.

>like
>giving a vampire +1 stealth and +1 strength. These are two good specials
>but are wasted by putting them on the same vampire because you will never
>use them together (okay maybe stealth rush).

Stealth rush wouldn't be a bad one. It would - of course - depend on
what the rest of the vampire looked like *but* at the same time,
remember how well Nose of the Hound has gone down. Stealth rush? No.
But flexibility, yes. You don't play it just for the stealth in the
first place, you play it because you want a rush, but you include it
over a competing card for that extra slot.

It wouldn't just have to be stealth rush, either. The vampire might
well make a good vampire to include a rush/diablerie deck. Yeah, you
get the stealth on the rush but you weren't really looking for that -
you get it on the diablerie action too, for instance, or any rescues you
undertake.

If it would well for a vote/rush clan, an unstoppable Archon deck could
be formed.

Some forms of bruise and bleed wouldn't say no to it. Some prefer to
play bruise and bleed, with the bleed as an attraction to get into
combat. Others prefer the bleed to be able to get through when they
need it. (This is one of the arguments against Archon Investigation
perenially (also Protected Racehorses) - that the bruise and bleed deck
wants to be able to get a BIG bleed through when it gets one through,
whereas a stealth bleed deck can often get little bleeds through
repeatedly.) For such a deck, having a spare +1 stealth might be worth
it. Even losing out a little on the disciplines can be good for the
right decks.

(One example of such a deck would be Watenda, in the weenie obf/pot
decks of old. His special was considered worth it by some, even though
he didn't have any pro-combat. Well, I say some. I mean Jasper
Philips.)

It can also really annoy some decks when a good vampire has a fight-back
special. They plan to take 1 damage from your strike - look at some of
the very precarious weenie rush decks - and when they find themselves
taking two...

Such unorthodox combinations would need some work to get off the ground,
yes. Whereas synergistic combinations would need a lot less work, so
you pay a little more.
